prose.article: Sardites refers to the family group descended from Sered, one of the sons of Zebulun. The word appears only once in the Old Testament, in Numbers 26:26, as part of the census of Israelite clans recorded in the wilderness. It functions as a gentillic noun — a label identifying people by their ancestor — and carries no broader semantic range beyond that genealogical meaning.

The KJV renders it variously as 'rebellion,' 'revolt,' 'wrong,' and even 'continual,' showing the translators struggled to pin it to one English concept. prose.def: A coat of mail or body armor worn by soldiers in battle.
